newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares steady, firm on domestic support.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares steady, firm on domestic support.

text.p: Domestic support held leading Russian shares steady, even nudging some stocks higher on Tuesday amid a lack of Western interest, traders said.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index inched up 0.68 percent to 557.99 after closing on Monday at 554.20. Total market turnover was a sturdy $71.4 million.
Traders said Russian money, previously concentrated in the government securities market, was flowing into equities as levels sank from last week's highs.

"You can feel a lack of Western institutional investor support on the market due to the vacation season, but Russian operators decided that this is the right time to jump on the end of the train," United Financial Group trader Igor Vain said.

National power company UES EESR.RTS ticked down to $0.4404 from $0.4435, while oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS was barely changed at $27.36 after $27.35. But Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS rose to $16.15 from $15.10.
"There is a myth about Russian money but it has become reality," said Alfa Capital's head of equity trading Dmitry Yershov. "I do not see any other more attractive financial instruments now."
But Vain said speculative trading was making the market volatile and saw prices fluctuating slightly over the rest of the week.

"The market is unpredictable, it isn't moving on fundamental analysis but on broker speculation," he said. "If we'd seen even a little selling pressure these (upward) moves wouldn't have been so easy."

While many analysts see Russian stocks rallying in the autumn after a possible cooling in August, Yershov said the possible profit-taking by Western investors could puncture the market bubble and trigger a decline.
"It's completely possible that this growth is a pyramid -- Russians will not have enough money and the West will walk away and not support the market," he said.
